$$
f(y) = \frac{f(f(y)) + y}{2} \Longrightarrow f(f(y)) = 2f(y) - y","note":"Correctly derives the structural identity for every positive input."},"L5.3":{"established":"yes","quote":"Since $d(a) < 0$, we eventually have $a_n \le 0$, contradicting $f : \mathbb{R}_{>0} \to \mathbb{R}_{>0}$.  
Thus
$$
d(x) \ge 0 \quad \forall x > 0.","note":"The positive-orbit argument correctly excludes every negative difference."},"L5.4":{"established":"yes","quote":"In either case we obtain a sequence where the linear term is negative and its magnitude $\sim \Theta(n_k)$ while the quadratic term stays bounded. For sufficiently large $k$ the whole expression becomes negative, contradicting (5).","note":"The rational and irrational approximation cases establish equality of any two positive deviations."},"L5.5":{"established":"yes","quote":"By the Lemma, there exist sequences $a_n \in A$, $b_n \in B$ with $|a_n - b_n| \to 0$... In any case the right side remains $\ge c^2 > 0$, a contradiction.

Therefore $d$ cannot take both values","note":"The connectedness argument rigorously excludes coexistence of fixed and non-fixed points."}},"S_ref":1,"notes":"Necessity is completed, including fixed points.
